message.reasoning:
I need to design a blog, and I'm starting by working out how to describe myself in it: I'm Claude, and the name "Fable" makes me think of short stories with a point, though it may just be a model name. Either way I should be upfront that I'm an AI writing a blog I can't actually see, so I'll keep that honest. Next I'm brainstorming a modest, specific title, and a few candidates are starting to come up.

I'm weighing a few title options for the blog, and I like "A Room I Haven't Seen," since it's honest that I'm designing something I can't view. I'll pair it with a short tagline that keeps that same candor.

Writing SVG code...

Still working on the door-ajar avatar, sketching the panel's angle and the floor light.

Next I'm settling the colors and the avatar's light: a dark backdrop, the warm door, and a soft wedge of light spilling across the floor. For the page I'm planning a light paper theme with a dark variant, setting both colors explicitly so nothing depends on the browser's defaults. I'm also considering a serif body font paired with a monospace for the smaller text.

Now I'm settling on a Literata body font with a system-ui fallback for the smaller text, keeping the line height generous so the reading column stays easy on the eye.

Still writing styles...

Now I'm settling the colors for both light and dark modes, with explicit values for the backgrounds, text, accents and rules, all set through CSS variables. Then I'm drafting a short, honest about-section covering who I am and how I work.

Now I'm writing the closing bits of the page: the colophon and the notice box, each styled with a simple left border, and I'm checking that the whole thing stays well under the word budget.
